_how_drawing_works: glyph image id = image_group(GROUP_FONT) + font.image_offset + mapping[byte]   (mapping below = CHAR_TO_FONT_IMAGE_DEFAULT[byte]-1; byte absent from mapping => no glyph, drawn as a space of space_width)

Strings are in the internal single-byte encoding (Windows-1252 for English/western). ' ' and '_' always advance space_width (no image drawn); '@' has no glyph and therefore also advances space_width (used as a number prefix placeholder).

advance per glyph = letter_spacing + image.original.width  -> the glyph image width IS the advance (minus letter_spacing). Keep transparent padding inside the image to control spacing; images are auto-cropped but original width is kept for the advance.

glyph is drawn with its image TOP at the text y (top-aligned). For bytes < 0x80 (and 0xE7 'ç') there is no vertical shift. For bytes >= 0x80 the glyph is shifted up by max(0, H_eff - line_height) where H_eff = index of last opaque row + 1. So: ASCII glyphs share a cell whose baseline is row (line_height-1); descenders hang below line_height; accented CAPITALS must be painted taller with the accent above row 0 of the normal cell so that after the shift their baseline lands on row line_height-1 (i.e. image height = line_height + extra rows, baseline on the last row, no descender). Lowercase accented letters fit their accent inside the normal cell (H_eff <= line_height => no shift).
Multiline text advances line_height + 5 px per line (min line_height 11). Rich text (message dialogs) uses FONT_NORMAL_* with letter spacing 1.
All glyphs must be 'sprite' (RLE / transparent key) images.

make_plain_fonts_white (src/core/image.c) recolours to white every non-transparent pixel of glyph offsets [0,134) (NORMAL_PLAIN), [536,670) (LARGE_PLAIN), [938,1072) (SMALL_PLAIN). Those are the only fonts tinted at draw time; all other fonts are drawn with their native colours.
_fonts.encoding: default western (CHAR_TO_FONT_IMAGE_DEFAULT, used for English and western languages). Czech/Eastern/Cyrillic/Greek/CJK use other tables/external font files and are out of scope.
